meta.title: Lattice surgery: splitting a logical qubit

paper.authors: I. Besedin, M. Kerschbaum, J. Knoll et al. (ETH Zurich)
paper.title: Lattice surgery realized on two distance-three repetition codes with superconducting qubits

meta.summary: A distance-three surface code on 17 transmons is split by lattice surgery into two distance-three repetition codes, which leaves them in a logical Bell state: ⟨Z_L1·Z_L2⟩ = +0.730 decoded and +0.998 postselected after the split, ⟨X_L1·X_L2⟩ = +0.56 postselected.
meta.program: The paper's gate sequence (its gate-sequence figure), transmon for transmon: logical |0⟩, four X and three Z stabilizer cycles, the split by measuring D2, D5 and D8, two Z cycles of each repetition code, and the data readout; no qubit is reset after its readout. Then the `decode_syndrome` system call on the decoder core, and the Pauli-frame update the paper applies in software as real pulses: X on L2's data (D3, D6, D9) when the decoded Z_L1·Z_L2 is −1. The system call level: the compiler lowers the inverse operation, a Bell pair by an X⊗X merge of two d = 3 surface-code blocks, against the twin's durations and the decoder's calibrated latency.
meta.twin: The 17 transmons at their chip positions (the paper's micrograph) with a coupler for every gated pair, the paper's gate times (48 ns single-qubit DRAG pulses, CZ 101.5 ns with its buffers), 300 ns readouts (the longest of its 175–300 ns), on the layer timeline derived from its 1.66 µs period between same-type cycles. One RISC-Q core per transmon at 500 MHz, a frame core and the decoder core.
findings: Every operation of both circuits ran inside its window on the twin: the stabilizer cycles, the split and the readout take 8.85 µs (Z·Z) and 8.89 µs (X·X), the paper's layer timeline on the controller's 2 ns grid.

In the same Lean run the decoder starts 0.29 µs after the last readout window closes, decodes the 36 detectors in 93.0 µs, and the three conditioned X pulses start 0.48 µs after its result. The paper applies this frame update offline; done in real time on this controller it costs 93.7 µs, about ten times the circuit.

Under the paper's simulation model the twin gives raw ⟨Z_L1·Z_L2⟩ = +0.228 (paper +0.189) and ⟨X_L1·X_L2⟩ = +0.213 (+0.255); decoded Z·Z = +0.575 with PyMatching and +0.570 with the compiled decoder, against the paper's +0.730 (its matching graph's weights are learned from the device's data); postselected +0.998 with 1.8% of shots kept and +0.501 with 2.1%, against +0.998 (5.5%) and +0.56 (6.3%).

The compiled decoder's correction equals PyMatching's on 88% (Z·Z) and 86% (X·X) of noisy shots: without resets each detector compares measurements two rounds apart, and union-find, which is not minimum weight, differs more often on that graph.

As a system call: the resource VM refuses the merge on the 17-qubit device (two d = 3 surface-code blocks reserve 18 data qubits, QUBIT_CAPACITY) and admits it on a 42-qubit machine: 820 timed operations in 302.8 µs, the decoder declared with its measured worst case. The paper fits 17 qubits because its two halves are repetition codes, which the compiler does not offer as a code.

One ZCU216 holds at most 14 RISC-Q cores (riscq/board.mjs, sized from RISC-Q's RTL and Vivado records), so this twin's 19 cores need at least 2 boards. The Lean run keeps them on one board's hub, so syndrome bits that would cross boards arrive without the about 0.6 µs a crossing costs on RISC-Q's board-to-board network.
limits: Readout lengths per qubit are not published (175–300 ns): every readout takes 300 ns. Per-qubit coherence is not published: T1 = 51 µs (the midpoint of 24–78 µs) and T2E = 50 µs for every qubit.
The noise is the paper's simulation model (depolarizing gates, readout flips, idling over each layer's time); leakage, crosstalk and the learned weights of the paper's matching graph are not modeled.
The paper does not state its control electronics: the controller is QuantumOS's RISC-Q model.

device.title: ETH Zurich 17-transmon surface-code device
device.basis: The circuit is the paper's gate sequence (Methods, its gate-sequence figure), qubit for qubit, on the chip positions of its micrograph. Single-qubit and CZ times are the paper's; the layer timeline is derived from its 1.66 µs period between same-type cycles and its eight steps per stabilizer measurement (meta.json derived_schedule). Readout lengths per qubit are not published (175–300 ns): every readout takes 300 ns. The control electronics are not stated in the paper: the controller is QuantumOS's RISC-Q model, one core per transmon, with a decoder core.

x90Ns.source: Besedin et al., arXiv:2501.04612, Methods, Idling and Single-Qubit Gates: "For single-qubit gates, we apply 48 ns derivative removal by adiabatic gate (DRAG) microwave pulses"

xNs.source: Besedin et al., arXiv:2501.04612, Methods, Idling and Single-Qubit Gates: "For single-qubit gates, we apply 48 ns derivative removal by adiabatic gate (DRAG) microwave pulses"

czNs.source: Besedin et al., arXiv:2501.04612, Methods, Two-Qubit Gates: "The average duration of the CZ gate is 101.5 ns."; the 20 ns buffers on each side are in the layer time, not the pulse

readoutNs.source: Besedin et al., arXiv:2501.04612, Methods, Qutrit Readout and Leakage Rejection: "resulting in durations ranging from 175 to 300 ns across the 17 qubits"; the longest of the range, for every qubit

resetNs.source: the paper: "We do not reset qubits after their readout" (no reset is played)

Z_L1 Z_L2 raw / decoded.source: "the expectation value of the Z_L1 Z_L2 observable increases from its raw value of 0.189(5) to 0.730(3)"

Bell fidelity raw / decoded.source: "we improve the Bell state fidelity from F_raw=0.382(2) to F_dec=0.546(2)"

Z_L1 Z_L2 postselected.source: "the postselected expectation value improves significantly to 0.998(1)"

X_L1 X_L2 raw / postselected.source: "the X_L1 X_L2 observable shows only a small increase from 0.255(5) to 0.56(2)"

postselection retention.source: "The fraction of retained experimental runs after postselection is 6.3% for the X_L1 X_L2 and Y_L1 Y_L2 observables, and 5.5% for the Z_L1 Z_L2 observable."

Bell fidelity postselected.source: "The Bell state fidelity for the postselected dataset is 0.780(6)"

process fidelity raw / decoded / postsel.source: "The resulting process fidelity for the raw outcome is 0.310(12). Decoding improves the process fidelity to 0.442(12). Postselection yields a process fidelity of 0.78(3), while retaining only 3.3% of the experimental runs."

arbitrary-state ZZ contrast decoded / po.source: "The highest contrast of 0.646(5) for the error-corrected observable and 0.97(2) for the postselected observable is obtained for Z_L1 Z_L2"

gate errors (RB / IRB).source: "we measure average single-qubit and two-qubit gate errors of (0.09+-0.05)% and (2.2+-1.7)%."

readout assignment fidelity.source: "The average two-state and three-state readout assignment fidelity is 98.5% and 97.5%, respectively."

noise.note: The paper's simulation model (its appendix): depolarizing 0.09% after one-qubit gates, 2.2% after CZ, 1.5% readout flips, and the idle Pauli channel 1 − exp(−t/T) with T_X = T_Y = 4·T1 and T_Z = T_φ over each layer's time, T1 = 51 µs (midpoint of 24–78 µs) and T2E = 50 µs (representative; per-qubit values are not published).

exactness.status: exact (text + App. Fig. A + App. Pauli Frame Update)

exactness.part: cycle order X,(Z,X)x3, split, Z,Z; m=3, n=2; readout of D2 D5 D8 in Z with the 4th X readout; final data readout with the last Z readout
CZ partners and their order in steps 2,3,5,6 for both stabilizer types, and which CZs are dropped after the split
exactness.status: reconstructed from Fig. 3a (TeX figs/fig_3a.png) at full resolution; every partner set reproduces the stabilizer supports; resulting Z_L1Z_L2 circuit distance 3 matches the paper's statement that the smallest undetectable logical fault has weight three

exactness.part: rotation angles (-pi/2, pi, +pi/2) of every single-qubit pulse
exactness.status: reconstructed from Fig. 3a box shading by pixel analysis against the legend; the sign convention of 'Y rotation' and its mapping to SQRT_Y vs SQRT_Y_DAG is assumed (Ry(t)=exp(-itY/2)). A different convention changes only constant outcome signs, not detectors or distances.

8-step structure exact; the pipelined readout is placed in the same layer as step 1 of the next stabilizer type, as drawn in Fig. 3a; the split readout and the post-split Z readouts are standalone layers as drawn. Real readout (175-300 ns) overlaps more than one 48 ns step; layer durations are derived (derived_schedule).
included as M on all 17 qubits after R (Fig. 3a 'Presel.'); hardware postselects on all-0, so it is not used in detectors (detector partners at rounds 1, 2 are this postselected 0)

paper's syndrome definition sigma_N = s_N s_N-1 with s from no-reset raw outcomes, i.e. m_k xor m_k-2; 24 Z detectors (sigma_0..sigma_5, matches source-data decoder graph) + 12 X detectors (cycles 2-4, matches App. Fig. F1). The paper's indexing of the split syndrome (sigma_4 with s_4 s_3, 1-based s) vs source data (sigma_0..sigma_5) is internally inconsistent; the physics is the same.

Stim observables are frame-updated parities. In the raw measurement record of the noiseless circuit Z_L1Z_L2 has parity 1 for the +1 state, because of the Ry(pi) echoes (5 on D4 and D6, 3 on D5) and the no-reset ancilla mapping; the paper reports the value after this known constant frame (see verify.txt (b)).

initial-state pattern exact (Fig. 4a: D1 D4 D6 D9 |0>, D2 D3 D7 D8 |+>, D5 |psi>); the preparation pulses are not given (only 'single-qubit gates'), minimal choices used: |+>=SQRT_Y, |->=SQRT_Y_DAG, |1>=Y, |+i>=SQRT_X_DAG, |-i>=SQRT_X. Only Stim-representable cardinal states; the paper's 45-degree states are non-Clifford. Detectors exclude the non-deterministic first-round weight-4 checks, as in the paper.
chip grid read from the labelled micrograph Fig. 1e (exact topology, photo-derived pitch ~1.85 mm)

sanity only: device-average errors from the text, idle channel of App. Simulation with representative T1=51 us, T2E=50 us; per-qubit / per-pair values are not published with qubit labels (source data fig_1f.csv lists unlabelled values)

decoding.mode: offline (post-processing); no real-time decoding, no feed-forward: Pauli-frame updates are virtual
decoding.decoder: minimum-weight perfect matching (blossom, pymatching); edge weights from syndrome correlation analysis of the experimental data (Spitz 2018); separate Z (bit-flip) and X (phase-flip) graphs
decoding.quote: we address using the blossom algorithm, implemented in the pymatching package
decoding.quote_frame: The virtual gates are performed by flipping the logical qubit observable outcomes in post-processing.
decoding.section: App. Error Correction for Tomographic Readouts; Lattice surgery on a distance-three surface code
decoding.leakage: runs with any leaked (|2>) readout are discarded; preselection discards runs with any qubit excited at the start

calibration.decoder: riscq/decoders/uf_decoder.c (union-find with peeling), compiled for a RISC-Q core, Lean model
